list.ai_navigation_and_perception: Apply whenever characters or enemies must move around obstacles, see or hear the player, patrol, chase, search or run behavior trees.
list.arcade_shooter: Apply when making a fixed-screen arcade shooter (Galaga, Space Invaders, Galaxian, Centipede): ship at the bottom, enemy formations that swoop and dive, waves, lives, high score.
list.art_style: Apply whenever the user asks for a look or art style (realistic, stylized, low poly, toon, retro, noir, painterly) or says a scene looks wrong.
list.builder: Apply whenever building objects, buildings, landmarks or scenes from parts: real-scale dimensions, generators, materials.
list.game_logic: Apply whenever making a scene playable: variables, rules, events, UI, players, combat, AI, spawners, saves.
list.game_ui: Apply when making any HUD, menu, inventory, shop, scoreboard or dialog: layout UI that looks like a polished web/game UI.
list.gameplay_ability_system: Apply when a task involves stats (health, shield, mana, stamina, speed), buffs and debuffs, damage over time, status tags (stunned, burning), abilities with costs, or a project that already uses Unreal's Gameplay Ability System (GAS).
list.outdoor_lighting: Apply whenever setting up or changing outdoor lighting: sun, sky, clouds, fog, exposure, time of day or weather.
list.pcg_graph_generation: Apply whenever a task involves repeating patterns or rules over space: scattering vegetation or rocks, roads and fences along paths, filling areas, grids of buildings, or spatial computation (distances, subdivision, filtering points). Not for one-off placements.
list.python_kit: Apply when a task needs many objects or many steps (levels, cities, landmarks, games with lots of rules) and you can run Python: use the unreal_kit shipped with the game to generate fast. Includes the full API, so no inspection is needed.
list.realistic_scene: Apply when the scene should look real (cities, streets, houses, interiors, landscapes, product shots): real scale, physical light and exposure, believable materials, detail and wear, eye-level cameras, and a screenshot review loop.
list.state_tree: Apply when a task involves the project's StateTree assets: running a designed behaviour (guard, door, boss phases, quest flow) on an actor, sending it events, or checking which state it is in.
list.vfx_placement: Apply whenever placing or spawning a visual effect: smoke, fire, explosion, sparks, dust, magic, impacts, ambient particles.
